statement: Let leafSeq(t) be the leaf value sequence of t: the list of values of all leaves of t in left-to-right order, where a leaf is a node Node(v, Null, Null). Formally, leafSeq(Null) = [], leafSeq(Node(v, Null, Null)) = [v], and leafSeq(Node(v, l, r)) = leafSeq(l) ++ leafSeq(r) whenever l != Null or r != Null (++ is list concatenation). Whenever the function returns a result r, r = true if and only if leafSeq(root1) = leafSeq(root2) (the two lists have equal length and equal entries at every index).
preconditions: root1 and root2 are trees of type Tree. Let n1 and n2 be the number of Node constructors in root1 and root2 respectively. Then 1 <= n1 <= 200 and 1 <= n2 <= 200, and every value stored in a Node of root1 or root2 lies in the range [0, 200].

statement: The function returns a result r (i.e., it does not fail, panic, or overflow) for every input satisfying the preconditions; r is a Bool.
preconditions: root1 and root2 are trees of type Tree. Let n1 and n2 be the number of Node constructors in root1 and root2 respectively. Then 1 <= n1 <= 200 and 1 <= n2 <= 200, and every value stored in a Node of root1 or root2 lies in the range [0, 200].

statement: Whenever leaf_similar(a, b) returns a result r1 and leaf_similar(b, a) returns a result r2, we have r1 = r2 (both true or both false).
preconditions: a and b are trees of type Tree. Let na and nb be the number of Node constructors in a and b respectively. Then 1 <= na <= 200 and 1 <= nb <= 200, and every value stored in a Node of a or b lies in the range [0, 200].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r = true, len(leafSeq(root1)) = len(leafSeq(root2)) and 1 <= len(leafSeq(root1)) <= 200, where leafSeq(t) is the list of leaf values of t in left-to-right order (a leaf is a node Node(v, Null, Null)).
preconditions: root1 and root2 are trees of type Tree. Let n1 and n2 be the number of Node constructors in root1 and root2 respectively. Then 1 <= n1 <= 200 and 1 <= n2 <= 200, and every value stored in a Node of root1 or root2 lies in the range [0, 200].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if leafSeq(root1) = leafSeq(root2) then r = true. Here leafSeq(t) is the list of leaf values of t in left-to-right order (a leaf is a node Node(v, Null, Null)).
preconditions: root1 and root2 are trees of type Tree. Let n1 and n2 be the number of Node constructors in root1 and root2 respectively. Then 1 <= n1 <= 200 and 1 <= n2 <= 200, and every value stored in a Node of root1 or root2 lies in the range [0, 200].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if leafSeq(root1) != leafSeq(root2) then r = false. Here leafSeq(t) is the list of leaf values of t in left-to-right order (a leaf is a node Node(v, Null, Null)).
preconditions: root1 and root2 are trees of type Tree. Let n1 and n2 be the number of Node constructors in root1 and root2 respectively. Then 1 <= n1 <= 200 and 1 <= n2 <= 200, and every value stored in a Node of root1 or root2 lies in the range [0, 200].

statement: Let leafSeq(t) be the list of leaf values of t in left-to-right order (a leaf is a node Node(v, Null, Null)). Whenever leaf_similar(a, b) returns a result r and leaf_similar(a', b') returns a result r', if leafSeq(a) = leafSeq(a') and leafSeq(b) = leafSeq(b'), then r = r'.
preconditions: a, a', b, b' are trees of type Tree. Each has between 1 and 200 Node constructors, and every value stored in a Node of any of them lies in the range [0, 200].

statement: Let leafSeq(t) be the list of leaf values of t in left-to-right order (a leaf is a node Node(v, Null, Null)). Whenever the function returns a result r and r = false, then either len(leafSeq(root1)) != len(leafSeq(root2)), or there exists an integer i such that 0 <= i < len(leafSeq(root1)), 0 <= i < len(leafSeq(root2)), and leafSeq(root1)[i] != leafSeq(root2)[i].
preconditions: root1 and root2 are trees of type Tree. Let n1 and n2 be the number of Node constructors in root1 and root2 respectively. Then 1 <= n1 <= 200 and 1 <= n2 <= 200, and every value stored in a Node of root1 or root2 lies in the range [0, 200].

statement: Define mirror(t) recursively by mirror(Null) = Null and mirror(Node(v, l, r)) = Node(v, mirror(r), mirror(l)). Let leafSeq(t) be the list of leaf values of t in left-to-right order (a leaf is a node Node(v, Null, Null)). Whenever leaf_similar(t, mirror(t)) returns a result r, r = true if and only if leafSeq(t) = reverse(leafSeq(t)), where reverse(L) is the list obtained by reversing L.
preconditions: t is a tree of type Tree with between 1 and 200 nodes, and every value stored in a Node of t lies in the range [0, 200].
